title: Deduplicated commit protocol for Optimize automation API and webhook flows
creator: Maya Patel
description: Introduce a deduplication-first commit protocol to make Optimize automation apply operations safe to retry and resilient to webhook replay or duplicate delivery. This ticket covers API changes, webhook handshake semantics, SDK helpers, server-side transaction fencing, and the migration path for older clients. Goal: avoid duplicate config changes, provide clear failure modes, and preserve observability for retries.
acceptance_criteria: New /optimize/v2/commits endpoint supports client-supplied operation_id and returns deterministic result for repeated requests with same operation_id.
Webhook delivery endpoint validates operation_id and returns 2xx for already-applied operations (idempotent behavior) while logging a duplicate_event metric.
SDKs provide a safe_commit helper that manages operation_id generation and retry backoff, integrating with existing auth and rate-limiting behavior.
Server enforces a configurable dedupe window (default 7 days) and exposes metrics: dedupe_hits, dedupe_misses, apply_conflicts, apply_duration.
Migration plan documented: older clients without operation_id continue to use legacy apply endpoint with best-effort dedupe and documented caveats.
End-to-end tests for exact-once semantics under simulated duplicate webhook deliveries and control-plane restarts.
Security review completed for accepting client-generated operation identifiers and for storage/rotation of operation metadata.
Rollout plan with Canary (5% traffic) -> Ramp (50%) -> Full (100%) with automated rollback on SLO regressions.
implementation_notes: API: add POST /optimize/v2/commits with body {operation_id, suggestion_id, dry_run, apply_plan_hash, expected_version?}. Server responds {status, commit_id, applied: bool, reason?}
Webhook: change callback contract to include operation_id in X-Optimize-Op header and expect 200 for duplicates. Provide X-Optimize-Dedupe: true header on duplicate acknowledgement.

Server: implement a small commit ledger table indexed by operation_id + customer_id. Ledger stores state: pending/committed/failed, commit_payload_hash, commit_result, timestamp. Use lightweight TTL to expire ledger rows after dedupe window.

Fencing: before applying, perform conditional compare-and-set based on suggestion_id version + apply_plan_hash to avoid blind overwrites. If mismatch, return 409 with diagnostics and a recommended reconcile action.
SDK: add SafeCommit helper that derives a RFC4122v4 operation_id by default but allows user-supplied ids for cross-process coordination. Expose options for timeout and max_retries.
Observability: emit structured logs and metrics for each commit lifecycle stage; trace ids should be propagated through webhook callbacks.
Backward compatibility: keep POST /optimize/v1/apply for older clients but mark deprecated in docs and route internally to new commit flow with server-generated operation_id.
Testing: simulate network duplicates, delayed webhook retries, and DB restarts to validate idempotency and correct dedupe metrics firing.
Scaling: shard ledger by customer_id mod N and use batched writes to Redis/primary DB for high-throughput customers (Dedicated).
